name: elf-shot

attributes.attribute: folkloric motif of tiny invisible arrows flung by fairies
one shot could bring down a cow
old name for the paralysis left by an elf-shot

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Elf-shot is a folkloric motif, also called elf-smitten. Fairies used tiny, almost invisible arrows against beasts and people. The arrows flew with great force and caused real damage. One elf-shot could bring down a cow. Those struck fell into partial or full paralysis. People still call that state by its old name, fairy stroke.
